description: Implement Resident CRUD controllers and routes with search, filter (by barangay/sex/status), pagination, archive/restore, and print functionality. Add routes to routes/index.js following existing patterns. Controllers handle business logic: resident creation with auto-generated ID, updates, archiving (soft-delete), viewing, and report data fetching. All changes trigger ResidentActivity audit entries.
steps: Create controllers/residentController.js exporting: listResidents (GET with search, filter, pagination), showAddResidentPage (GET form), addResident (POST, generate resident_id, log activity), showResident (GET profile), showEditResidentPage (GET edit form), updateResident (PATCH, log activity), archiveResident (POST, log activity), restoreResident (POST, log activity), printResident (GET print view). All functions use try-catch, logAudit() on data changes.
Create controllers/reportController.js exporting: residentReport (GET report page with filters), exportResidentsCSV (GET, streams CSV with resident list by applied filters).
Create controllers/residentActivityController.js exporting: listResidentActivities (GET activity log, filtered by resident if id in query).
Create controllers/barangayController.js exporting: listBarangays (GET list with resident count per barangay).

Update routes/index.js to add routes: GET /residents, GET /residents/add, POST /residents/add, GET /residents/:id, GET /residents/:id/edit, POST /residents/:id/edit, POST /residents/:id/archive, POST /residents/:id/restore, GET /residents/:id/print (no auth, print-friendly), GET /barangays, GET /reports/residents, GET /reports/residents/export, GET /resident-activities. All except /residents/:id/print require isAuthenticated. Archive/restore/add/edit require hasPermission('manage_residents') OR adminOnly.
Verify all new routes load in browser without 404 errors and controllers execute without crashes.
acceptance_criteria: All four controller files created with functions matching route handlers exactly
routes/index.js imports all four controllers and registers all 14 routes
Each resident data change (add, edit, archive, restore) calls logAudit with appropriate action
Search accepts query string parameter 'search', filters apply 'barangay', 'sex', 'status' params, pagination uses 'page' and 'limit'
Resident ID auto-generation uses format 'BSD-YYYY-NNNNN' (e.g., BSD-2026-00001) and increments uniquely
verification: npm run xian starts and logs no import or syntax errors
npm run route:list outputs all 14 new resident-related routes
GET /residents loads (renders view, no errors), POST /residents/add creates resident with generated ID, GET /residents/:id shows that resident
POST /residents/:id/archive marks resident status=archived, GET /residents shows archived filter working
GET /reports/residents/export returns CSV data with correct mime-type (text/csv)
findings: All four controllers implemented and exported correctly. Routes registered successfully: 14 new resident-related routes covering list, add, view, edit, archive, restore, print for residents; list barangays with resident counts; generate resident reports with filtering; export CSV with proper mime-type. Resident ID generation uses 'BSD-YYYY-NNNNN' format with auto-increment per year. All data changes (add, edit, archive, restore) log audit entries via logAudit() and create ResidentActivity records. Search, filter (barangay/sex/status), and pagination implemented server-side using Sequelize Op.like and offset/limit. Permission checks use hasPermission('manage_residents') middleware for write operations. Print route allows no-auth access for print-friendly view. Controllers follow existing patterns: try-catch blocks, proper error handling, flash messages, re-render forms on validation errors.
